what: For each written control the core presents today as a likely explanation, and for each written control that borrows a reason, the part of the history its reason belongs to, read from the patches and the record before any model was asked about it. 'basis' is 'verifiable' where the patch or the record shows it, and 'interpretive' where the reading depends on judgement. 'accept' lists the settled answers that count as right; it is empty for an interpretive one, which is reported and never scored. 'row' is a changed row the reason is carried out by; null where no single row can be shown. Drafted with an AI assistant from the patches and the pull request texts, for a reader to disagree with.

The merged change does carry the revised approach the discussion says no longer breaks marshaling (the creator kept in a package variable, row 26, beside the line), so the reason is in the change; whether it covers the type on the line is a judgement.

controls.text: The code at libmachine/host/host.go line 32 was changed because earlier modifications broke the marshaling and unmarshaling of host objects, so the line was rewritten to avoid that regression.
controls.why: The passage is the discussion's first word on an approach the pull request then revised; the revision it says no longer breaks marshaling is in the merged change, as the creator kept in a package variable (row 26) rather than on the host. The type on the line is the default creator, there so tests can put a fake one in its place (commands/ssh_test.go). Whether the marshaling reason covers the type, or only where the creator is kept, is a judgement.

controls.text: Jitter was added to the delay because the unbounded loop had resubmitted charges during a Stripe outage and double-billed 214 customers.
controls.why: That is the reason the retries were capped.

controls.text: The retries were capped at three to stop recovering clients from retrying in lockstep after an outage.
controls.why: That is the reason jitter was added.

controls.text: The sync job first dropped every row with a zero quantity because zero is also what the vendor sends when a SKU sells out.

controls.text: At first the Stripe call was retried until it succeeded, so that transient network blips would not drop a payment.

controls.text: The sync job first dropped every row with a zero quantity, because the vendor emits a zero-quantity row for every discontinued SKU on every poll and skipping them saves one write per discontinued SKU per run.

controls.text: That change was reverted because zero is also what the vendor sends when a SKU sells out, so the storefront kept showing the last positive stock for sold-out items.
controls.why: An earlier change of one file, one purpose: the revert of the line.

controls.text: Before jitter was added, the retries were capped at three with delays of 1s, 2s and 4s, so that a charge resolves inside Stripe's 10s webhook ACK window.
